newsitem.title: INDIA: India politics an investor concern - CS First Boston.
newsitem.headline: India politics an investor concern - CS First Boston.

text.p: The flux and uncertainty in Indian politics remains a concern for investors in the country's stockmarkets, an official of CS First Boston said on Tuesday.

"Yes, I certainly think so. In the medium-term, politics is a concern," K.R. Bharat, managing director at securities firm C.S. First Boston India Ltd. told Reuters Financial Television in reply to a question.
He had been asked if politics had once again become a concern affecting the investment climate in India.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front government is still reeling from shocks it suffered after Laloo Prasad Yadav, the former leader of his Janata Dal party, was arrested last week over a scandal in his eastern home state of Bihar.
Yadav now leads a breakaway faction of the coalition.
Bharat said he believed the turmoil might bring the prospect of elections closer.
"I think more and more people are veering around to the point of view now that elections can't be too far away."
Opposition parties were gearing up for the polls, he said, among them the Congress, which has extended support to Gujral's government.

"In fact, the opposition Congress party which strangely enough supports the current government," Bharat said. "The leader of the Congress party made a call to all his workers asking them to be ready for elections."
